entities.summary:
Gregory of Langres, also known as Gregory of Autun, was a Gallo-Roman prelate born around 446 in Saone-et-Loire, France, who later became count of Autun and bishop of Langres from 506 to 539. He played a significant role in the politics and religion of the Western Roman Empire during its decline. As a prominent figure, Gregory was instrumental in shaping the Christian Church in Gaul, which later became an integral part of the Catholic Church.

Gregory's significance extends beyond his own lifetime, as his legacy influenced the development of Western Christianity. He was canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church and celebrated on January 4th, marking a testament to his enduring impact on the faith.

The legacy of Gregory of Langres serves as a reminder of the complex and often contentious nature of Christian politics in the Western Roman Empire, highlighting the intricate relationships between church leaders, local authorities, and the broader imperial context.
